decision.explanation: Finding 1: The source states that ponatinib is the only approved TKI capable of inhibiting BCR-ABL carrying the gatekeeper T315I mutation, and that T315I is associated with resistant or relapsed CML. This directly supports the claim that BCR::ABL1 with ABL1 T315I predicts sensitivity/response to ponatinib in CML. Finding 2: The PACE trial report notes that patients with the T315I mutant had a 74% major cytogenetic response rate, supporting clinical response to ponatinib in a population that included CML patients. The evidence is sufficient to support the supplied claim as written.

citations.quote: Ponatinib is the only approved TKI capable of inhibiting BCR-ABL with the gatekeeper T315I kinase domain mutation, known to be the cause for 20% of resistant or relapsed CML cases. . . . Although the overall structure remains similar in many ways to other approved TKIs, the ability to potently inhibit native BCR-ABL, BCR-ABL-T315I, and many other mutant forms of BCR-ABL made ponatinib a highly versatile drug with great potential moving into clinical evaluation. . . .

The Phase II Ponatinib Ph+ALL and CML Evaluation (PACE) trial enrolled 449 patients: 267 with CP-CML, 83 with accelerated phase (AP)-CML, and 94 with blast crisis (BC)-CML or Ph+ALL . . . Responses were observed for each of 15 mutations present at baseline for CP-CML patients, and 26 unique mutations in total. Response rates were similar for those with and without mutant BCR-ABL, with MCyR occurring in 56% of all patients, 49% of patients with native BCR-ABL, 64% for those with one mutation, 62% for those with two or more mutations, and 74% for those with the T315I mutant. . . .
